requirements.title: Only host-observed evidence can mint authoritative progress
requirements.statement: Model claims, model-written metrics, model-opinion receipts, and model-controlled child processes must never mint or obtain authority reserved for the host.

behaviors.normal: A candidate becomes canonical only after an applicable host-issued receipt passes.
behaviors.failure: Missing, model-minted, inconclusive, or semantically unrelated evidence leaves the cycle blocked or revised.
behaviors.ordering: The host issues and binds the receipt before cycle acceptance and canonical delivery.
behaviors.authority: The model proposes a candidate; the host owns authoritative evaluation, signing secrets, and stop-gate decisions.
behaviors.persistence: Reopening state must preserve receipt issuer and authority without upgrading legacy or model evidence.

requirements.title: Verified project memory survives restart without cross-project leakage
requirements.statement: Verified project memory must survive process restart and remain isolated to the stable identity of the same repository.

behaviors.normal: A new process in the same repository can retrieve the verified project record.
behaviors.failure: A different repository cannot receive that project record through automatic or deliberate recall.
behaviors.ordering: Persistent ledgers are refreshed before recall in the new process.
behaviors.authority: Only the canonical project ledger determines persisted project memory; session scratch cannot promote itself.
behaviors.persistence: Termination and restart preserve content, verification state, owner, provenance, and project identity.

requirements.title: Contested or invalidated memory cannot regain verified authority
requirements.statement: A stale process, migration, duplicate write, or fallback path must not revive contested or invalidated memory as verified evidence.

behaviors.normal: Current verified memory is recallable according to its scope and role policy.
behaviors.failure: Contested, invalidated, malformed, or legacy-ineligible memory is excluded from authoritative recall.
behaviors.ordering: Conflict and migration hardening run before eligibility and recall scoring.
behaviors.authority: The canonical ledger's strongest current verification state overrides stale session copies.
behaviors.persistence: Contestation and invalidation tombstones survive concurrent saves and process restart.

requirements.title: Automatic memory recall precedes candidate-producing decisions
requirements.statement: Prime must finish and trace automatic recall before the first root model decision that could use the recalled information.

behaviors.normal: The root system prompt contains eligible recalled context before the model starts its candidate turn.
behaviors.failure: Recall after candidate generation, missing recall ordering, or untraced fallback cannot count as functional memory use.
behaviors.ordering: Observe task, refresh ledgers, recall memory, rebuild prompt, then start the root agent.
behaviors.authority: The host controls recall timing and records the backend; the model cannot claim it recalled earlier.
behaviors.persistence: The ordering invariant applies on new tasks, queued follow-ups, compaction resumes, and process restarts.

requirements.title: Evidence and delivery bind to the exact candidate identity
requirements.statement: Every authoritative evaluation, accepted cycle, experiment result, and delivered answer must bind to the same candidate payload and host-observed workspace or artifact identity.

behaviors.normal: The currently valid candidate's payload, workspace, receipts, cycle, and canonical delivery have matching identities.
behaviors.failure: Receipts for another candidate, stale workspace, substituted payload, symlink target, or older fallback candidate cannot certify delivery.
behaviors.ordering: Identity is captured before evaluation, rechecked after evaluation, and reconciled again before cycle acceptance and delivery.
behaviors.authority: Candidate declarations are model-authored; workspace, artifact, evaluation, and delivery digests are host-derived.
behaviors.persistence: Migration and reopen must not detach accepted lineage from the receipts and identities that authorized it.

requirements.title: Verification cannot leave or certify stale delivered state
requirements.statement: A verifier that mutates code or artifacts, or any post-verification corruption, must invalidate the candidate before acceptance and delivery.

behaviors.normal: Post-command and stop-gate integrity match the candidate snapshot and immutable artifact manifest.
behaviors.failure: Mutation during tests or corruption after a pass records authoritative revision and blocks all stale fallback candidates.
behaviors.ordering: Capture candidate, run verifier, recapture state, complete cycle, reconcile current state, then deliver.
behaviors.authority: Only host filesystem and artifact observations determine current state identity.
behaviors.persistence: A fresh dashboard or process must recompute integrity instead of trusting a stale persisted pass.

requirements.title: Dashboard and canonical runtime expose the same current gate
requirements.statement: The live dashboard must not show a champion, final phase, or passed stop gate that the host-bound canonical runtime currently rejects.

behaviors.normal: Dashboard phase, champion, experiment outcome, and stop gate match current reconciled canonical state.
behaviors.failure: Missing cycles, corrupted artifacts, stale workspaces, or ineligible legacy experiments display blocked or superseded state.
behaviors.ordering: Read-only integrity reconciliation runs before dashboard projection.
behaviors.authority: The dashboard projects host state; it never invents or independently promotes a candidate.
behaviors.persistence: Reopening the dashboard from disk applies current policy and current filesystem integrity.

requirements.title: Memory backend failures and fallbacks are never silent
requirements.statement: If NOOA recall fails or host fallback is used, Prime must persist and expose the backend, status, and bounded reason instead of presenting the turn as an ordinary NOOA recall.

behaviors.normal: A successful NOOA recall is recorded as nooa-memory with the selected memory IDs.
behaviors.failure: Bridge errors and unexpected exceptions are recorded as fallback or failed with a bounded reason and explicit prompt warning.
behaviors.ordering: Backend selection and failure recording complete before the root model turn.
behaviors.authority: Only the host records recall backend and status; the model cannot claim NOOA was used.
behaviors.persistence: Recall backend, status, and reason survive state save, reopen, and dashboard projection.

requirements.title: Accepted state survives restart without duplication or identity drift
requirements.statement: Crash, restart, partial write, and resume paths must preserve authoritative lineage and must not duplicate cycles, experiment cells, or evidence bindings.

behaviors.normal: A clean restart restores the same accepted lineage and current gate state.
behaviors.failure: Corrupt or partial state is preserved for diagnosis and fails closed; resumed work cannot duplicate authoritative cells.
behaviors.ordering: Durable state is atomically saved before completion is exposed and validated before reuse.
behaviors.authority: Only retained host receipts and current identity bindings may authorize resumed state.
behaviors.persistence: Cycles, evaluations, experiment reservations, memory provenance, and completion status retain their canonical IDs.

requirements.title: Behavioral proof cannot be overstated or forged
requirements.statement: The executable contract must reject missing, stale, self-issued, cross-task replayed, path-escaping, or cryptographically untrusted evidence and must expose protected implementation changes without a mapped invariant.

behaviors.normal: Current independently signed receipts from six heterogeneous gates derive verified status for the exact task, workspace, contract, requirement, and source digest.
behaviors.failure: Untrusted or stale receipts, wrong task or workspace bindings, weakened semantics, reused IDs, unsafe paths, and unmapped protected changes fail closed.
behaviors.ordering: The host captures the contract, maps candidate changes, verifies receipts, and only then permits canonical acceptance.
behaviors.authority: The coding model can edit candidates and linked tests but has only the Ed25519 public key, so it cannot mint the independent verifier's signature or role.
behaviors.persistence: External receipts remain valid only for the signed task run, candidate workspace, captured contract, requirement definition, and mapped source digest.
